docs.purpose: Gives a trade contractor the full detail view for one lead they are considering bidding on — a construction permit or a committee-of-adjustment application — including its address, timing estimates, cost estimates, neighbourhood demographics, how many other contractors are also tracking it, and whether they have saved it themselves.
docs.data_story: It reads 6 tables — `permits`, `cost_estimates`, `neighbourhoods`, `trade_forecasts`, `lead_views` and `coa_applications` and writes nothing. Its response shape is **unmeasured** as a pick-by-name whitelist — it passes rows through, spreads a row into a computed object, or assembles the payload dynamically, so there is no single list naming what leaves the server. It is called from 2 places: `src/features/admin-flight-center/api/useLeadDetail.ts`, `mobile/src/hooks/useLeadDetail.ts`.
docs.under_126: Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `QUERY`. It declares its `database.reads[]` with named columns, its response projection as an explicit whitelist, its auth class, its rate bucket and its staleness — and `outputs.writes` is forced to `"none"`. Its `consumers[]` becomes the edge list of the fan-out graph — the join nothing in this estate holds today.

notes: Two branches depending on whether the id is a permit or a CoA lead; all SQL lives in src/lib/leads/lead-detail-query.ts (LEAD_DETAIL_SQL and COA_LEAD_DETAIL_SQL). Response is built by mapper functions (toLeadDetail/toCoaLeadDetail) constructing a typed object rather than an explicit whitelist array. Both queries bind the viewer's uid as ::uuid, with the dev-bypass non-uuid sentinel normalized to NULL first via isUuid() to avoid a Postgres cast error. Called via template literals from both web and mobile. | MEASURED 2026-09-15: AUTH CLASS: 'authenticated' — AUTHENTICATED_API_ROUTES contains '/api/leads' (src/lib/auth/route-guard.ts:124) and the prefix test at :165-167 matches. A MERELY-AUTHENTICATED caller (any user_profiles row with a trade) sees, for ANY permit or CoA in the database: full address parts, lat/lng, work description, lifecycle phase/stall, cost_estimates estimated_cost + tier + range_low/high + modeled_gfa_sqm, and the neighbourhood income block (avg/median household income). There is NO entitlement check on this route even though `ctx.subscription_status` is available (src/lib/auth/get-user-context.ts:149) and the sibling /api/parcels route is documented as enforcing exactly such a gate (src/features/leads/api/error-mapping.ts:22-29). No object-level authorization either: the WHERE clause is the permit id alone (lead-detail-query.ts:132-133) — unlike the flight-board detail route, there is no `lead_views.user_id = ctx.uid` scoping, so any authenticated user can enumerate every permit by id.
